Air Environment
The information presented in this section is a summary of the Air Quality Report prepared by the Wisconsin Department of Transportation for the Airport Spur and circulated to the Department of Natural Resources in October 1975. If more detailed information is desired the Air Quality Report-Airport Spur should be consulted.
In consultation with DNR, the cognizant Indirect Source Review agency, the air quality assessment meets the requirements of Wisconsin Administrative Code NR 154, "Indirect Source Rules," effective July 1, 1975 and satisfactorily responds to their letter of comment to the draft environmental statement as included in Section &. The report was prepared in accordance with the Highway Program Manual, "Air Quality Guidelines", dated November 26, 1974.
The proposed Airport Spur project involves a new highway corridor that will directly connect existing Interstate 94 with the airport terminal facilities at General Mitchell Field. This section will be concerned with assessing the impact that this proposed route will have on air quality in the immediate area and for individual receptors located adjacent to the project.
The proposed Airport Spur is a new indirect source located within the Standard Metropolitan Statistical Area of Milwaukee. (An indirect source is defined as the construction of a highway facility which attracts mobile source activity that results in emissions of a pollutant for which there is a national standard). An annual peak hour traffic volume of 1200 or more vehicles per hour can be expected on the new facility within 10 years of construction. Volumes in excess of this peak hour traffic require the filing of a notice of intent to construct under Wisconsin Administrative Code, Chap. NR 154.
